title: Compute Edge Betweenness
description: For each edge in the graph, calculate its betweenness centrality: the number of shortest paths between all pairs of nodes that pass through that edge. Use Brandes' algorithm for efficiency.

title: Find Edge with Highest Betweenness
description: Identify the edge(s) with the maximum betweenness score. If multiple edges tie for the highest score, select one according to a deterministic or random tie-breaking rule.

title: Remove the Edge
description: Remove the selected edge from the graph. This progressively disconnects the graph into smaller components, each representing a community at that stage of the algorithm.

title: Recompute Betweenness
description: After each edge removal, recompute the betweenness centrality for all remaining edges. The removal of an edge changes shortest paths, so betweenness scores must be recalculated.

title: Repeat Until Stopping Criterion
description: Continue removing edges one at a time until all edges are removed, or stop when a desired number of communities is reached. The algorithm produces a hierarchical dendrogram of community splits.

title: Select Best Partition
description: From the dendrogram, choose the partition that maximizes modularity Q. This determines the optimal number of communities automatically.
